newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

In London the March white sugar contract took a late tumble as it went off the board and expired at $305.70 per tonne, down $2.0. May remained unchanged at $301.40 per tonne. Traders said they expected as much as 3 cargoes of white sugar to be delivered against the contract mainly from the European Union but possibly also Poland.

In New York raw sugar futures closed barely weaker in heavy trade focused on speculative liquidation and options activity ahead of Friday's March expiry. March lost 2 points to close at 10.64 cents/lb, while May gave up 4 points to close at 10.61 cents/lb. The outer months lost 3 points. Our second estimate of the world sugar balance 1996/97 had no impact as it was very much in line with our previous projection.

There was talk of heavy Indonesian purchases of Thai white sugar. In 1996 Thailand exported 666,000 tonnes of white sugar to Indonesia, up from 333,000 tonnes shipped the previous year and 91,000 tonnes shipped in 1994. However, total Indonesian import requirements in 1996/97 (May/April) and 1997/98 are forecast to decline due to expected higher production, mainly in 1997/98

FINLAND - Sugar exports in November 1996 amounted to 7,014 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 2,309 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first two months of 1996/97 (October/November) up to 12,094 tonnes, hardly changed from last year's 11,265 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 49,721 tonnes against 6,763 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October/November 1996 were Estonia with 5,102 tonnes whites compared to 2,911 tonnes and Latvia with 2,499 tonnes compared to nil.

CHINA - Sugar imports continue to trail behind those of last year. Total imports in December 1996 reached 93,369 tonnes, raw value, which was up from the November figure of 45,611 tonnes but sharply down on the December 1995 imports of 33,865 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996/97 (September/December) up to 421,668 tonnes compared to 1.112 million tonnes imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 1.945 million tonnes against 2.907 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in September/December 1996 were Australia with 228,793 tonnes raws against 297,066 tonnes, Cuba with 132,590 tonnes, down from 168,953 tonnes and Thailand with 29,382 tonnes against 226,498 tonnes. There were no sugar exports in December 1996 so that the September/December 1996 total stayed unchanged at 162,609 tonnes compared to 394,483 tonnes in September/December 1995. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 830,203 tonnes compared to 540,004 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in September/December 1996 were Pakistan with 62,499 tonnes against nil, Saudi Arabia with 39,481 tonnes compared to 102,100 tonnes and Hong Kong with 25,228 tonnes against 38,860 tonnes.

Taiwan Sugar Corporation confirmed buying 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar. No further details were available. Furthermore, trade sources reported that Pakistan had bought about 10 to 12 cargoes of whites for March/April shipment over the past two weeks from various trade houses.
